notes.meaning: 'Had relations' is the Bible's polite way of speaking about married love. Even after the fall, God still blessed Adam and Eve with children. Eve gives thanks that the Lord helped her bear a son. The name Cain sounds like the Hebrew word for 'gotten.' Some think Eve hoped Cain was the promised child who would crush the serpent (Genesis 3:15). If so, she was sadly wrong.

Abel's name means 'breath' or 'vanity,' a reminder of how short and fragile life is. Both brothers had real work to do: Abel kept flocks and Cain farmed the land. Older writers saw in this that God wants every person to have useful work. Both jobs were honest and good.

Worshiping God is not a new idea. It goes back to the first family. Cain brings some of his crops as a gift to the Lord. Many think God himself had taught Adam's family to bring offerings, and that they had been brought up to worship him. 'In the course of time' may point to a set time, perhaps a day of rest and worship.

Abel gave the best he had: the firstborn of his flock and the richest parts. God looked first at the person and then at the gift. Abel came with an honest heart and offered in faith (Hebrews 11:4). Cain was only going through the motions. Many older writers add that Abel's animal offering showed he knew he was a sinner who needed God to cover his sin (that covering is what 'atonement' means). Cain was angry and his face fell, which showed envy and resentment toward God and his brother.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: The Hebrew word for 'offering' can mean any gift, including crops. On this view, the giver's attitude mattered, not whether the gift was grain or an animal.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: The text does not say why Cain's offering was turned down. Following Augustine, Catholic teaching has said that Cain gave God some of his goods but kept back his heart.

notes.meaning: God gently reasons with Cain to warn him before worse things happen. He asks Cain to look honestly at why he is angry. If Cain does what is right, he will be accepted. The way back was still open. But sin is pictured as a wild animal crouching at the door, ready to pounce, and Cain must master it. Many older writers read the last words another way: Abel will still respect Cain as the older brother, so Cain has no reason to be jealous.

differ.view: God's command to master sin does not show that people can do it in their own strength. Only the grace of the Holy Spirit makes it possible.
God really put the remedy within Cain's reach. Sinners are lost not because no Savior is offered but because they will not use what God has placed in their power.

notes.meaning: Cain's anger grew into murder. He used friendly words to get Abel alone in the field, and there he killed him. The Bible later says Cain did it because his own deeds were evil and his brother's were right (1 John 3:12). The first person ever to die was a righteous man, and the first to die for his faith.

God already knew what had happened. He asked so that Cain could confess. Instead, Cain told a bold lie and then talked back to God. In truth, we are called to care for our brothers and sisters. Shrugging off that duty is speaking Cain's language.

God sees every wrong, even when no one else complains. Abel could not speak, but his spilled blood 'cries out' to God for justice. God cares for his people even after they die. The New Testament says Jesus' blood 'speaks a better word than Abel's' (Hebrews 12:24): Abel's blood cried for justice, while Christ's blood cries for pardon.

Cain is the first person God curses directly. The ground that soaked up Abel's blood now turns against him and will no longer give him good crops. He will be a restless wanderer, haunted by his guilty conscience wherever he goes. Even so, there was mercy: God did not end his life at once, which gave him time to repent.

Cain complains about his punishment, not about his sin. He shows no sorrow for what he did and does not ask for forgiveness. He fears being cut off from God's presence and the place of worship. He also fears that relatives who learn of the murder will kill him.

God protects Cain's life. This was not to reward Cain. It was to hold back more killing and to keep revenge in God's own hands. 'Sevenfold' means a full and severe punishment. God gave Cain a sign or mark, but the Bible does not tell us what it was.

Cain left the place where God met with his family and turned his back on worship. He settled in Nod, which means 'wandering.' The name fits the restlessness in his heart. Those who leave God cannot find true rest anywhere else.

Cain's wife was one of Adam's daughters. This was before God's later law forbade marrying close family. Cain built a city and named it after his son. Older writers saw this as Cain trying to feel safe and settle down on earth, apart from God's people. This Enoch is not the godly Enoch of chapter 5.
Cain's family line is listed quickly, by name only. The godly line in chapter 5 is described in more detail. The list leads to Lamech, the seventh generation from Adam through Cain.
Lamech is the first man said to take two wives. This broke God's first pattern for marriage, where one man and one woman become 'one flesh.' It began in Cain's godless family line.

Lamech's sons started new ways of life. Jabal began tent-dwelling herding, Jubal music, and Tubal-cain metalworking. 'Father' here means the first one, or founder. These skills are real gifts from God, even when given to people who do not follow him. Still, older writers note sadly that nothing is said here about anyone fearing or serving God.

Lamech brags to his wives in what may be the oldest poem in the Bible. He boasts that he kills anyone who hurts him. He twists God's mercy to Cain into an excuse for more revenge: if Cain is avenged seven times, Lamech will be avenged seventy-seven times. God had meant to limit bloodshed, but Lamech wants to multiply it. Sin is getting worse.

After all this grief, God comforts Adam and Eve with another son. Seth's name sounds like 'granted' or 'appointed.' Eve sees him as God's gift in place of Abel. Through Seth the godly family line continues, the line from which the promised Savior would one day come.

Seth's son Enosh has a name that means 'man,' a reminder that people are weak and frail. Then people began to call on the name of the Lord. This means they worshiped him together, openly and on purpose. While Cain's line turned away, God stirred up his people to worship again, almost like a first revival.
